env.world: A finite population \(\mathcal U_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) of labeled units carries a completely deterministic, composition-indexed potential-outcome schedule: for each arm \(z\in\mathcal Z=\{0,1\}\), each candidate group \(A\in\Omega_{n,M}=\{A\subseteq\mathcal U_n:|A|=M\}\) of the fixed common size \(M\ge2\), and each \(i\in A\), a real number \(Y_{i,n}(z,A)\) with \(\sup_{n,i,z,A}|Y_{i,n}(z,A)|\le B<\infty\). No superpopulation and no sampling law over units is introduced. The slice \(\Omega_{n,M}\) is equipped with the uniform law, which supplies the averaging operator \(\mathbb E_nf=\binom nM^{-1}\sum_{A\in\Omega_{n,M}}f(A)\), the inner product \(\langle f,g\rangle_n=\mathbb E_n[fg]\) and the norm \(\|f\|_n^2=\langle f,f\rangle_n\) on \(L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\). The group-level schedule is the arm table \(h_{z,n}(A)=M^{-1}\sum_{i\in A}Y_{i,n}(z,A)\), with centering \(h_{z,n}^{\circ}=h_{z,n}-\mathbb E_nh_{z,n}\) and uniform-slice arm variance \(V_{z,n}=\langle h_{z,n}^{\circ},h_{z,n}^{\circ}\rangle_n\).

env.world: The uniform \(M\)-slice \(\Omega_{n,M}\), for \(n\ge2M\), is regarded as the vertex set of the Johnson association scheme. Its function space \(L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\) carries harmonic degree subspaces \(\mathcal H_{n,0},\ldots,\mathcal H_{n,M}\) with \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_n\)-orthogonal projections \(\Pi_{n,k}\), and the normalized Kneser disjointness operator \((\mathsf K_nf)(A)=\binom{n-M}{M}^{-1}\sum_{C\in\Omega_{n,M}:C\cap A=\varnothing}f(C)\), which averages \(f\) over a uniform group disjoint from \(A\) and acts on \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\) by the scalar \(\lambda_{n,k}\). The derived quadratic functionals of the arm table are the ordered-disjoint covariances \(C_{ab,n}=\langle h_{a,n}^{\circ},\mathsf K_nh_{b,n}^{\circ}\rangle_n\) for \(a,b\in\mathcal Z\), their contrast \(C_{\tau\tau,n}=C_{11,n}+C_{00,n}-2C_{10,n}\), and the degree-one arm-difference energy \(E_{\tau,1,n}=\|\Pi_{n,1}(h_{1,n}-h_{0,n})\|_n^2\).

env.world: The two-stage dense random-group design on the population of S1. First an ordered tuple \(\mathbf A_n=(A_{n1},\ldots,A_{nG_n})\) is drawn uniformly from the ordered tuples of pairwise-disjoint members of \(\Omega_{n,M}\), so that \(N_n=MG_n\le n\) units are grouped and the grouped-unit fraction satisfies \(N_n/n\to\rho\in[0,1]\); no birthday-scale condition on \(N_n^2/n\) is imposed. Then, independently of \(\mathbf A_n\), a group-treatment vector \(\mathbf Z_n\in\{0,1\}^{G_n}\) is drawn uniformly among vectors with exactly \(G_{1n}\) treated groups, \(G_{0n}=G_n-G_{1n}\), \(p_n=G_{1n}/G_n\to p\in(0,1)\); treatment is shared within each realized group. The assignment is the only randomness. This world carries the observed group means \(H^{\mathrm{obs}}_{ng}=Z_{ng}h_{1,n}(A_{ng})+(1-Z_{ng})h_{0,n}(A_{ng})\), the estimand \(\tau_n=\mathbb E_nh_{1,n}-\mathbb E_nh_{0,n}\) and its difference-in-means estimator \(\widehat\tau_n=G_{1n}^{-1}\sum_gZ_{ng}h_{1,n}(A_{ng})-G_{0n}^{-1}\sum_g(1-Z_{ng})h_{0,n}(A_{ng})\) with exact design variance \(\sigma_n^2=\operatorname{Var}(\widehat\tau_n)\), the independent-group leading variance \(R_n=V_{1,n}/p_n+V_{0,n}/(1-p_n)\), the within-arm sample variances \(s_{z,n}^2\) and the scalar equal-group CR2 statistic \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}=s_{1,n}^2/G_{1n}+s_{0,n}^2/G_{0n}\). The one-realization observation channel is \(\mathcal O_n=(\mathcal U_n,\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n,\{Y_{i,n}(Z_{ng},A_{ng})\})\), on which an arbitrary variance statistic \(\widehat S_n(\mathcal O_n)\) may be computed. Triangular arrays of such rows satisfying growth, fraction, envelope and scaled-variance conditions form the uniformity class \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) with constants \(B\) and \(c_\sigma\). There are no superpopulation nuisances.

substrate_survey.reason: `FiniteDesign` + the whole `E`/`Var`/`Cov`/`Pr`/`ind`/`map` finite-sum algebra is exactly the design-based layer this paper works in; `Cov_linear_comb` and `Var_linear_comb` are the workhorses of the exact variance identity.

`completeRandomization` is simultaneously the uniform \(M\)-slice law (S1) and the second-stage complete randomization of group labels (S3); `completeRandomization_incl(_pair)` are the needed CRE moments.
`Var_sampleMean` gives \((1/M-1/n)\operatorname{popVar}\) for a uniform \(M\)-subset mean, which is exactly the additive-schedule arm-variance identity (1) of `prop:rademacher-mixture-separation`.

`prodDesign` + its independence/variance lemmas carry BOTH the product Rademacher schedule priors of S4 and the independent two-stage combination of S3: `prodDesign` is parameterized by a dependent family `alpha : iota -> Type*` (`Product.lean:43,49`), so a two-element index family realizes the heterogeneous (partition-tuple, treatment-vector) pair with no new combinator, and `FiniteDesign.map` transports it to the product type.

`chebyshev`, `TendstoInProb` and the closure/Slutsky lemmas are the exact convergence-in-probability engine for the CR2 frontier and the sparse corollary; they are already indexed by an `n`-sequence of designs.
`toMeasure` / `integral_toMeasure` / `toMeasure_real_setOf` bridge the finite design layer to the measure-theoretic `Causalean.Stat.tvDist` used by the impossibility theorem.
`tvDist`, `one_sub_tvDist_le_test` and `two_point_lower_bound_of_tvDist_le` are precisely inequality (24) and the all-statistic step (25) of the impossibility proof.

`Var_tauHat` and `E_Shat` are the same proof pattern (complete-randomization indicator moments through `Var_linear_comb`; unbiasedness of an observed sample variance under a \(\{0,1\}\) selection family) but for FIXED cluster values; here the per-group scores are random slice functions, so the double sum retains an ordered-disjoint-pair covariance factor. Adapted, not reused verbatim.
The pairing `P` is fixed and only the within-pair coin is randomized; this paper's first-stage randomness is the pairing/partition itself, which is precisely the object under study.

`compound` models stage-two randomization within coordinates conditional on stage one; here the two stages are independent and stage one is a random partition of the unit set, not a per-coordinate design, so the independent product `prodDesign` over a two-element dependent stage family (pushed forward by `FiniteDesign.map`) is used instead — reuse, not a new combinator.
`clusterDesign` takes the unit-to-cluster map `clus : U -> C` as fixed data; the whole point here is that the cluster map is random and finite-pool competitive.

Proof plan: write the centered estimator as a linear combination of `Z_g / p_n * x_{1g} - (1 - Z_g) / q_n * x_{0g}` and apply `FiniteDesign.Var_linear_comb` / `Cov_linear_comb`; the diagonal gives `R_n / G`; the off-diagonal needs (a) the complete-randomization second-order label moments, EXACT reuse of `completeRandomization_incl` / `completeRandomization_incl_pair`, and (b) the stage-one pair marginal `marginal_uniform_ordered_disjoint_pair` from [def:random-partition-design], which identifies each off-diagonal group-pair expectation with `crossCov a b` via the `orderedDisjointPairDesign` bridge; `C_{01} = C_{10}` comes from t1. The CR2 expectation is the sample-variance expansion `E s_z^2 = V_z - C_{zz}` under an exchangeable ordered-disjoint m-tuple. thm:qv-diagonal-impossibility.notes: Paper-owned, in scope; the hardest proof in the plan, kept `defer_tier:false` because it is the paper's headline lower bound. Conjuncts: existence of high-prior-probability deterministic schedule supports `Gamma_n^j` all of whose Cartesian diagonal selections lie in `DenseScheduleClass`; vanishing total variation between the two CONDITIONED one-realization mixture laws; uniform convergence of `G_n sigmaSq` on each support to `d_same` / `d_ind`; the design-region certificate (probability `1 - o(1)`, both first-observed-sign support probabilities `>= 1/4`, conditional variance `>= 3/4`); and the all-statistic bound `liminf sup over the class of Pr(|Shat/sigmaSq - 1| > eps) >= 1/2` for some `eps > 0`. Proof plan: t8 gives the rowwise prior limits and the exact equality `P^{same,0} = P^{ind,0}`; the diagonalization picks `k_n -> infinity` with `H^j(Gamma_n^j) -> 1`; conditioning costs at most `H^j((Gamma_n^j)^c)` in total variation (layer-cake over the observation kernel), so the triangle inequality gives `||P^same - P^ind||_TV -> 0`; the sign-nondegeneracy region comes from `1{|q - 1/2| > 1/4} <= 4|q - 1/2|`; the final step is the testing inequality. REUSE (verified signatures): `Causalean.Stat.tvDist` on `FiniteDesign.toMeasure` (finite spaces, discrete sigma-algebra, so every statistic is measurable), `Causalean.Stat.one_sub_tvDist_le_test` (`1 - tvDist mu nu <= mu.real A + nu.real A^c`) is literally the paper's inequality (24), and `Causalean.Stat.two_point_lower_bound_of_tvDist_le` (`(1-c)/2 <= max (P0.real {s <= |est - theta0|}) (P1.real {s <= |est - theta1|})` given `2s <= |theta0 - theta1|` and `tvDist P0 P1 <= c`) is the all-statistic step (25), applied with `est = G_n * Shat`, `theta_j = d_j`, `s` just below `(d_same - d_ind)/2`; `FiniteDesign.toMeasure` / `toMeasure_real_setOf` / `integral_toMeasure` bridge the finite design layer to it. ANALOGOUS REFERENCE for the witness-to-lower-bound wrapper: `Causalean/Estimation/MinimaxATE/Reduction/Witness.lean:{twoPointWitness_lower_bound, twoPointWitness_quarter}`; gap to bridge: there the two laws are a fixed pair of laws with close TV, whereas here they are CONDITIONED mixtures over deterministic-schedule supports and the parameter is the exact design variance `sigmaSq`, which varies over the support — hence the uniform-on-support convergence (5) is needed before the wrapper applies.
